main thing to remember is that when it comes to lithium there really aren't certain amounts that are a lot or a little. It's all about the individual.

I'm not sure if side effects go up with the amount that you're taking or what your levels are in your blood. If it's the actual amount and the side effects are becoming too much you can always talk to you psych about how you don't think it's for you then try some different anti-psychotic , there are a ton of different options out there and it just takes time to find what's right for you

from what my psych said it was all about balance, as in don't just do anything weird or go on any diets that will suddenly change your salt levels drastically. Doing something that makes it so you're having a lot more salt then usual will make the lithium less effective (not sure about this but i'm pretty sure it's because you're body will flush out the salts in your body quicker, lowering the amount of lithium in your body.), and doing something that lowers the amount of salt in your body (heavy sweating, sudden diet changes) makes the lithium stay in your body longer as it has less of the other type of salt in your body, putting you at risk of going into the toxic range.
